messages:
incident-bot: PAGER -> @tim-oncall: Performance alert (p99) for /v1/generate in us-east-1. p95 680ms -> 2.1s, p99 1.4s -> 4.2s; elevated streaming stalls observed. Auto-mitigation suggestion: route 20% to fallback-model.

tim-oncall: acked. I'm looking. @infra-bot can you confirm if there were any infra events in us-east-1 around 17:08? :eyes:

infra-bot: No control-plane failures. Noted GPU pool spike on dedicated-workers-3 at 17:05 (cpu steal + queue depth). No node reboots.

tim-oncall: checking runtime traces now. Looks like tokenizer/preproc tails have a long tail. Correlating requests with JSON-mode tool-schema heavy prompts.

maya: I see a few recent deploys to preproc-service at 17:02 (small PR to template expansion). Could be related. Rolling back to previous revision now for a canary.

jack: paging data from observability: top slow path is prompt-template-render -> tokenizer expansion -> tool-schema assembly. Most affected requests include large JSON-mode blocks (structured tool calls). Example trace id: trace-0x9a3fd.

oliver: logs show repeated 429 retries inside preproc (backpressure). Stack snippet:
```
preproc: queue_wait=312ms; render_time=1.1s; tokenizer_time=2.3s; err=null
```

leah: customer-facing impact: streaming clients reported stalls around 17:04, some clients dropped connections after 10s. I can surface a quick incident banner if we expect >30m.

tim-oncall: Quick mitigation plan:
1) Route 35% traffic to fallback-model (lower tokenization overhead) immediately.
2) Scale preproc-service replicas + add extra preproc-worker pods (x3).
3) Disable JSON-mode strict parsing for streaming clients temporarily (devex rollback flag).
4) Rollback preproc deploy from 17:02 if latency persists.

sara: I'm on the routing runbook. Applying route rule now: `redwoodctl traffic shift --service=frontend --route=/v1/generate --to=fallback-model --percent=35 --region=us-east-1`

devex-bot: Feature flag changed: jsonmode.strict_parsing=false for frontend in us-east-1 (applied by @sara). Will take ~15s to propagate.

infra-bot: Scaling preproc-service: `kubectl scale deploy/preproc-service --replicas=12 -n inference-us-east` (was 6). Starting.

jack: also bumping tokenizer pool size on runtime nodes via infra API to increase parallel decode workers.

oliver: warm cache job started for prefix-KV caches for top 200 templates: `jobs/warm-kv-templates --top=200 --region=us-east-1` (queued)

maya: rollback applied for preproc-service to revision r2023 (pre-17:02). Canary to 10% now.

tim-oncall: monitoring p95/p99. Baseline before mitigation was p95 2.1s p99 4.2s. Current sliding window:
- 17:07 p95=1.6s p99=3.8s
- 17:09 p95=1.2s p99=2.9s

leah: customer impact update: 14 customers experienced increased tokenization latency, 3 had active streaming disconnects. Reached out to top-2 enterprise contacts with heads-up.

pm-anna: thx. Preparing incident banner: short note + ETA for next update in 20m.

tim-oncall: Can someone check if any heavy tool-schema prompts coincide with specific tenants? Use request attribute `metadata.tenant_id` and look for size>8k prompt payloads.

jack: scanning... found a pattern: large tool-schema embedding for tenant t-87 and a few anonymous high-throughput clients. t-87 has many JSON-mode tool calls with long arrays.

leah: flagged t-87 in support queue. Sending them a note to throttle/optimize while we stabilize.

devex-bot: With jsonmode.off, some clients will see less strict validation; QA mitigations: ensure no data loss for streaming tokens.

tim-oncall: Good. Live metrics now show p95 down to 420ms, p99 820ms at 17:12. Streaming error rate dropping.

incident-bot: UPDATE: Latency regression partially mitigated by routing (35%) + preproc scale + jsonmode toggle + rollback. Current severity: High -> Under Control. Continue monitoring for 30m, then transition to postmortem.

oliver: note: tokenizer CPU still shows occasional spikes on node g4-xxl-07 at 17:11; investigating hot-loop in template-expander. Putting a temp guard to cap per-request template recursion to 5.

maya: temp guard applied via config: `TEMPLATE_MAX_RECURSION=5` to preproc configmap; rolling restart to pick up.

tim-oncall: handoff: I'll stay for 15m then hand to @jack for follow-ups. Jack, you'll own the post-incident triage doc (include prompt template regression test set + JSON-mode evals).

jack: ack. I'll own the postmortem. Assigning initial actions:
- root cause hypothesis: recent template expansion change + unbounded JSON-mode validation created O(n^2) work for large toolschema arrays.
- short-term: keep jsonmode.off, cap recursion, keep scaled replicas until autoscale re-evaluated.
- longer-term: add circuit-breaker in prompt builder and add template complexity tests to CI.

leah: putting incident banner live now. Noting affected tenants and mitigation steps.

pm-anna: Customer comms draft in #customer-updates. Will align with legal for wording for enterprise notices.

tim-oncall: marking this thread for postmortem. If anything regresses I'll re-open pager. Thanks everyone for fast responses. :heart:

incident-bot: INCIDENT -> resolved (mitigated). Final metrics snapshot at 17:14: p95 130ms, p99 780ms; streaming error rate back to baseline. Postmortem assigned to @jack. ETA for postmortem: 48h.

sara: adding runbook note: "if preproc p99 > 2s -> consider jsonmode toggle + route 30% fallback + scale preproc by x2". PR open: infra/runbooks#452

jack: adding immediate follow-ups to backlog: add tool-schema size guard, add template complexity CI, add tenant telemetry to flag oversized prompts. Will ping eng-ml for quantization guidance for tokenizer.

maya: will prepare a small revert PR explanation in changelog and link to postmortem.

tim-oncall: closing thread. Please ping if you see any regressions. :heart:
